description: Four SEM micrographs (secondary-electron contrast) of boundary areas in the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel annealed for 1 h at (a) 900 °C, (b) 1000 °C, (c) 1100 °C and (d) 1200 °C; each panel has a white box in the top-right stating temperature and time, and a black scale bar. (a), 10 µm bar: large equiaxed grains separated by thin bright boundaries, with an orange arrow labelled "boundary κ" pointing to one such boundary; darker banded regions occupy the bottom and top of the field. (b), 10 µm bar: similar large-grain structure, boundaries appear as brighter, more continuous films labelled "boundary κ", with sparse fine white particles in the matrix. (c), 5 µm bar (highest magnification): a bright boundary junction with an arrow labelled "boundary κ"; sub-micrometre white particles and a few dark pits are scattered within the grains. (d), 15 µm bar: two contrasting regions — left, a large α grain with dense needle- and plate-shaped precipitates labelled "FCC particles in α"; right, a grain containing an even denser network of bright platelets; an orange arrow labelled "boundary κ" marks the bright intergranular film. No numeric property values are printed; the panels document boundary κ-carbide films and quench-formed FCC particles.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph, label '900 °C, 1 h', scale bar 10 µm. Large equiaxed grains with thin bright grain-boundary films; orange arrow labelled 'boundary κ' points to one boundary. Dark banded regions at the bottom (and partly top) of the field.

SEM micrograph, label '1000 °C, 1 h', scale bar 10 µm. Large grains separated by brighter, continuous boundary films; orange arrow labelled 'boundary κ'. A few small white particles and rare dark pores in the matrix.

SEM micrograph, label '1100 °C, 1 h', scale bar 5 µm (highest magnification). A bright grain-boundary junction with orange arrow labelled 'boundary κ'; numerous sub-micrometre white particles and a few dark pits inside the grains.

SEM micrograph, label '1200 °C, 1 h', scale bar 15 µm. Left: a large α grain containing dense needle- and plate-shaped precipitates labelled 'FCC particles in α'. Right: a grain with an even denser network of bright platelets. Orange arrow labelled 'boundary κ' marks the bright boundary film near the top.

observations.observation: All four panels carry a top-right white label giving annealing condition: (a) 900 °C, 1 h; (b) 1000 °C, 1 h; (c) 1100 °C, 1 h; (d) 1200 °C, 1 h.
Scale bars are printed as 10 µm in (a), 10 µm in (b), 5 µm in (c) and 15 µm in (d), so panel (c) is the highest-magnification view.
An orange arrow with the text 'boundary κ' is drawn in every panel, pointing to a bright thin boundary film between large grains.
The bright boundary films appear continuous along grain boundaries in (a)–(d), i.e. at all four annealing temperatures from 900 °C to 1200 °C.
Panel (d) contains the blue text label 'FCC particles in α' over a large α grain filled with needle-shaped and plate-shaped precipitates.
In (d) the grain on the right side of the boundary shows a much denser population of bright platelet-like particles than the labelled α grain on the left.
Fine white particles (sub-micrometre) are scattered inside grains in (b) and (c); their identity cannot be resolved at the supplied resolution.
The caption states the panels show SEM micrographs of 'some boundary areas' in the specimen annealed at 900, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C.
The citing text states that κ-carbide is found along some boundaries between large α grains in the α area over the annealing range 900 °C to 1200 °C, as shown in Fig. 10(a)–(d).
The citing text states the boundary κ-carbide is believed to form during quenching when the annealing temperature exceeds the κ-carbide dissolution temperature, between 850 °C and 900 °C.

The citing text states that in the specimen annealed at 1200 °C there are needle-shaped or plate-shaped particles in some large α grains (Fig. 10(d)), forming during quenching with basically an FCC structure.
The citing text states the boundary κ-carbide seen in Fig. 10 cannot be detected by XRD, probably because its fraction is too small.
The citing text states the needle/plate-like particles compete for Mn or C with boundary κ-carbide, tending to disappear when approaching the grain boundary.

unreadable_items: Identity/composition of the fine sub-micrometre white particles inside grains in (b) and (c) is not resolvable from the micrographs
The faint striated contrast within individual grains (possibly etching or polishing relief) cannot be interpreted from the pixels alone
Panel (a): the darker banded constituent at the bottom of the field is unlabelled, so its phase identity cannot be determined from the image
